mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 3% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% and remains >3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not sustain the level for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coincides with stronger consumer demand, as measured by HOUST, and predicts positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 130,000 and HOUST is above 2,000 for the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined signal (Pearson IC < 0.05), or one proxy moves in the opposite direction of the other during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 (real private consumption) over three months indicates weakening demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar 20-day windows when GDPC1 declines by >2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 117 signals supply-side weakness, which precedes negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO falls by >5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) rises above 5.5% for three consecutive months during a tightening cycle, S&P 500 20-day forward returns turn negative due to risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% and remains >5.5% for three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the UNRATE trigger, or the regime is not a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS and RSAFS (retail and financial activity) indicates robust labor market and consumer confidence, predicting positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies show simultaneous strength (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) below 191 for two months suggests disinflation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as markets price in rate cuts.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 60-day moving average during the CPI decline.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) exceeds 2,200 for two consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it signals resilient construction activity and supports positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when HOUST remains above 2,200 for two months in a recessionary regime.
